subChunks.title: Microservices vs Monolith

storyBeats.text: The Academy once had a single Grand Spellbook. When it grew too large, they split it — the Combat Library, the Alchemy Vault, the History Archives. Each could grow and be updated independently.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Don't reach for microservices on day one. A well-structured monolith is often faster to build and easier to operate. Microservices trade development simplicity for operational flexibility — make that trade consciously.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Print a comparison: for each of 3 attributes, print whether a Monolith or Microservices is simpler. Use format: "[attribute]: Monolith|Microservices".
guidedPractice.hint: Deployment and debugging are simpler with a Monolith. Granular scaling is simpler with Microservices.

tests.label: Comparison
tests.expected:
Deployment: Monolith
Granular scaling: Microservices
Debugging: Monolith

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: When would you choose a monolith over microservices? What is the main operational cost of microservices?

questions.prompt: What is the primary benefit of the Circuit Breaker pattern in microservices?
options: Prevents cascading failures when a downstream service is unavailable
Routes traffic to the nearest service
questions.answer: Prevents cascading failures when a downstream service is unavailable
questions.explanation: Circuit Breaker (e.g., Resilience4j) stops calls to a failing service and returns a fallback, preventing system-wide failure.

subChunks.title: Inter-Service Communication

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Synchronous calls are a wizard shouting across the hall for an answer. Async messaging is leaving a scroll in the mailbox — the recipient reads it when ready. Choose based on whether you need an immediate answer.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate async messaging: create a simple MessageQueue with publish(String message) and consume(). Publish three messages and consume them in order.
guidedPractice.hint: Use a LinkedList as the backing queue. publish() adds to the queue, consume() polls and prints.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Compare synchronous and asynchronous inter-service communication. When would you choose each?

questions.prompt: Which communication pattern provides the best resilience when a downstream service is temporarily unavailable?
questions.explanation: Message queues decouple producer from consumer. If the consumer is down, messages wait in the queue — no data loss.

subChunks.title: Service Discovery & API Gateway

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: The API Gateway is the Academy's front gate — all visitors enter here. It checks credentials, routes to the right tower, and shields the inner workings from the outside world.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate routing: given a map of service routes, write route(String path) that returns the service name for a given path prefix. Return "unknown" if no match.
guidedPractice.hint: Iterate the routes map entries. If path.startsWith(entry.getKey()), return entry.getValue(). Return "unknown" if none match.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is an API Gateway? List three responsibilities it can handle for all services.

questions.prompt: What does 'lb://' in Spring Cloud Gateway route configuration indicate?
options: Load-balanced — Spring Cloud will resolve the service via Service Discovery
Local binding — the service is on localhost
questions.answer: Load-balanced — Spring Cloud will resolve the service via Service Discovery
questions.explanation: lb://SERVICE-NAME tells the gateway to look up the service in Eureka and load-balance requests across instances.

subChunks.title: Distributed Tracing & Saga Pattern

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: In a distributed system, a single purchase involves five services. If step three fails, you must undo steps one and two — compensating transactions are the rollback mechanism of microservices.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate a choreography saga step: given a list of saga steps (strings), process each in order. If a step contains "FAIL", print "Compensating: " + step for all completed steps in reverse order.
guidedPractice.hint: Track completed steps in a List. On FAIL, iterate completed in reverse and print "Compensating: " + each.

tests.label: Saga
tests.expected:
Completed: CreateOrder
Completed: ProcessPayment
Failed at: FAIL:ReserveInventory
Compensating: ProcessPayment
Compensating: CreateOrder

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the Saga pattern. Why can't distributed microservices use traditional database transactions (2PC)?

questions.prompt: What is a compensating transaction in the Saga pattern?
options: An action that undoes a previously completed step when a later step fails
A transaction that runs concurrently to speed up processing
A read-only query that checks saga state
A retry mechanism for failed transactions
questions.answer: An action that undoes a previously completed step when a later step fails
questions.explanation: Compensating transactions are the distributed equivalent of rollback — they reverse the effects of already-committed steps.
